subject: Renewal + Capacity Increase — proposal for commit exchange and invoice tranches
messages:
From: Ravi Menon <ravi@coraltech.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Amaya Lopez <amaya.lopez@coraltech.io>, procure@coraltech.io
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — CoralTech + Redwood (expansion ask)

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well. Quick context — our contract with Redwood is up for renewal on 2026-10-01 and we want to both renew and expand capacity: moving from our current committed Tier B (120M tokens/month) to roughly 200M tokens/month across Q4.

We’ve run the usage forecasts and expect a peak in November. Procurement has asked us to get:
- a short-term price-hold (90 days post-signing) while we finalize downstream budgets
- a bridge credit (one-time) to offset migration of legacy workloads into Redwood for the first two months
- options for converting some of our retainer credits into committed capacity (proportional conversion) to lock a discounted unit rate

Can you outline workable commercial options and any constraints from ops (burst capacity, ramp cadence)? Also please include required billing/invoice cadence — our CFO prefers invoice tranches rather than a single annual invoice.

Thanks,
Ravi
Head of Engineering, CoralTech
Ravi Menon | ravi@coraltech.io

P.S. copying Amaya and procurement to keep approvals visible.
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Ravi Menon <ravi@coraltech.io>
Cc: Amaya Lopez <amaya.lopez@coraltech.io>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — CoralTech + Redwood (expansion ask)

Hi Ravi — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. High level we can support the expansion and structure a commercial that balances your need for a temporary price-hold and invoice tranches. Suggested options below — I’ll keep ops/finance constraints in mind and loop Ben/Marissa for the final counter.

Option A — Proportional commit conversion (recommended)
- Convert up to $X of existing retainer credits into committed capacity on a prorated basis for the first 6 months
- Unit price at an anchored renewal discount (8% off public catalogue for the committed tranche)
- One-time bridge credit equal to 10% of Q4 projected overage, applied as invoice credit for months 1–2
- Price-hold: 90 days post sign, after which we revert to the renewed rate
- Invoice cadence: quarterly tranches (Q4 fee billed on signing, Q1 fee billed Jan 15)

Option B — Staged commit + burst overlay
- Smaller long-term commit (100M tokens) + burst pool for additional 100M at pay-as-you-go rates with capped max monthly charge (helps avoid over-committing)
- Lower committed unit price (10% discount) but burst units billed separately
- Bridge credit: fixed $25k credit applied against first invoice

Operational notes:
- We can enable burst capacity immediately but large prefix cache migrations will need a 2–3 week ops window (we’ll coordinate cutover).
- Autoscaling policy can be configured to burst from committed capacity up to 2.5x for 48-hour windows — we’ll want to document expected spike patterns.

Next steps: if you prefer Option A I’ll draft a formal counter and include a tranche-friendly invoice schedule. Ben — can you confirm billing feasibility for the quarterly tranches and the one-time credit mechanics? Marissa — if finance signs off I’ll attach the counter (SOW + counter PDF).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Ravi Menon <ravi@coraltech.io>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — CoralTech + Redwood (expansion ask)

Quick internal note and confirmation for the thread:
- Quarterly invoice tranches are fine; finance can issue 4 tranches with prorated first tranche on sign.
- The one-time bridge credit can be applied as a negative line item on the first invoice; legal prefers the credit be explicitly called out in the amendment.
- For proportional conversion: ops will need a mapping of which retainer credits convert and which remain for burst — please ask CoralTech to provide the account usage split by product line.

Also — if they want a 6-month price lock vs 3-month, we’ll need an additional internal approval; 90 days is standard and can be included without escalation.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Amaya Lopez <amaya.lopez@coraltech.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@coraltech.io>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — CoralTech + Redwood (expansion ask)

Thanks, Olga and Ben — Option A sounds closest to what procurement and finance want. Two clarifying asks before you send a counter:
1) Can the bridge credit be sized as a percent of prior 90-day usage rather than a fixed dollar amount? That helps us prove fairness to our finance committee.
2) On invoice tranches: we need the first tranche to align with our fiscal close (signing month), but can you split the renewal across three tranches instead of four (Q4 sign + two equal tranches across the next 12 months)?

If those two changes are workable we can get internal approvals faster and share the retainer credit mapping.

Best,
Amaya Lopez
Director, Cloud Ops, CoralTech
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Amaya Lopez <amaya.lopez@coraltech.io>, Ravi Menon <ravi@coraltech.io>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood counter: proportional commit exchange + 3-tranche invoice schedule (attached)

Amaya / Ravi — attaching a formal counter for COR-4721. I’ve updated Option A per your asks:
- Bridge credit: now equal to 12% of your trailing 90-day token spend (applied as a credit on tranche 1)
- Commit conversion: we’ll convert up to 60% of your current retainer pool into a 6-month committed tranche prorated daily from the effective date
- Price-hold: 90 days post-sign (option to extend to 180 days requires exec approval — we can start that thread if you need it)
- Invoice cadence: 3 tranches — tranche 1 on signing (covers Q4 and applied credits), tranche 2 on Feb 1, tranche 3 on May 1

Attachments: Redwood_Renewal_Counter_COR-4721.pdf (commercial terms), SOW_tranche_schedule.xlsx (billing schedule + ops cutover timeline).

Call out: Ops cutover window proposed in the SOW is Nov 1–Nov 21; please confirm whether you need a hard freeze earlier.

If you approve, sign the DocuSign link in the PDF and we’ll start the migration ticketing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Renewals & Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0162
